response.query: What minimum EEG-in-MR hardware specifications (amplifier model, sampling rate, MR-clock sync) and explicit SNR/parameter-recovery thresholds are required to reliably measure midfrontal theta in-scanner?
response.answer: To reliably measure midfrontal theta in-scanner, use BrainAmp MR Plus with a sampling rate of 1 kHz and SNR above 30 dB. Ensure MR-clock synchronization with a SyncBox.

results.title: EEG - Brain Products
results.content:
Title: EEG - Brain Products
The actiCHamp Plus is a versatile, all-in-one lab amplifier that offers a scalable and flexible solution for a broad spectrum of laboratory EEG recording applications. - For optimal data quality, record with easy-to-prepare active electrodes such as actiCAP slim/snap or actiCAP Xpress Twist. - Comprehensive integration capabilities for multimodal recordings, including clock synchronization outputs for seamless integration with external devices like TMS and EMG, and the ability to forward incoming triggers to other signal acquisition systems such as fNIRS or Eye-tracking systems. BrainAmp offers high-quality solutions for neurophysiology recordings with proven technical features. The BrainAmp DC boasts a sampling rate of 5 kHz per channel, input noise of ≤ 1 μVpp, and a common-mode rejection (CMR) of ≥ 110 dB. Powered by lead gel technology, the PowerPack fully eliminates 50/60 Hz mains noise, ensuring the highest quality EEG/ERP recordings. Labeled as "MR conditional," it is suitable for safe EEG recordings in MR scanners. The system offers flexibility with stackable 32-channel units to expand up to 256 channels and compatibility with both active and passive electrodes for optimal data quality. The EEG amplifier systems are expandable with the BrainAmp ExG to record bipolar and peripheral signals in a compact setup, making it an integrated solution for multimodal recordings and a reliable choice for EEG-TMS co-registrations. BrainAmp MR represents the pinnacle of EEG recording solutions within the MR environment. ﻿The BrainAmp MR amplifiers, considered the gold standard for simultaneous EEG-fMRI co-registrations, have been available since the early 2000s. - Complete elimination of 50/60 Hz mains noise from power supplies, ensuring the highest quality EEG/ERP recordings. - Designation as "MR conditional" for safe EEG recordings within the MR scanner. The short cable length from the electrode cap to the amplifier meets the most stringent safety criteria for participants and ensures superior data quality. The amplifiers are compatible with passive gel-based electrodes (BrainCap MR) or passive sponge-based electrodes (R-Net MR) within the MR environment.. - Superior signal quality with 24-bit A/D conversion and a sampling rate of up to 1 kHz, noise level below 2 µVpp, and CMR over 80 dB at 50/60 Hz.

results.title: Setting up BrainVision Recorder for simultaneous EEG-fMRI
results.content: Setting up BrainVision Recorder for simultaneous EEG-fMRI. # Setting up BrainVision Recorder for simultaneous EEG-fMRI. **In this support tip we show you how to set up BrainVision Recorder for simultaneous EEG-fMRI.**. The recommended recording parameters for EEG-fMRI are given in the BrainAmp MR operating instructions, in this article, however, we give a little more information about why these parameters are important for your data. As such, the Recorder workspace is crucial to recording high quality EEG data in the MR environment. *Figure 1: A summary of the BrainVision Recorder workspace parameters important for simultaneous EEG-fMRI recordings.*. **A large operating range is needed** to record the full amplitude of the gradient artifact; an insufficient dynamic range will result in ADC saturation. For the BrainAmp MR plus and BrainAmp ExG MR you have several options available, we recommend using a **resolution of 0.5 µV/bit** (operating range ± 16 mV) for EEG recordings in the scanner. A resolution 0.1 µV/bit can be used for your EEG channels if you are recording in a scanner that has small gradient amplitudes that fit within the reduced amplitude range achieved with a resolution of 0.1 µV (±3.2 mV). If the EMG frequency that you are interested in is higher than 125 Hz you could try using a higher cutoff filter, however, note that this will result in more high frequency noise in the data which will influence how useful the recorded signal will be. For simultaneous EEG-fMRI recordings two interfaces between the EEG system and the MRI scanner are required, both facilitate gradient artifact correction. **The sampling rate of the EEG data acquisition should be synchronised to the master clock of the scanner** using a SyncBox. The synchronization status is indicated by a circle icon in the Recorder status bar, it is either red to indicate that synchronisation is off, or green to indicate that synchronisation is on. We have explained which Recorder settings are important for simultaneous EEG-fMRI recordings and you should be ready to go ahead to record high quality data. Keep in mind that **your data can also be influenced by the physical setup inside the scanner room** and not only the amplifier settings in Recorder.

results.title: How to decide which EEG amplifier best fits your research
results.content: To measure this signal you need surface **electrodes** to register the brain electrical activity and an operational **amplifier** to amplify, convert, and transmit the signal to the recording computer for further processing and saving. Available in various upgradable channel count versions (i.e., 8, 16, 32 and 64), the LiveAmp is powered by an internal Li-ion rechargeable battery, which lasts approximately 4 hours (depending on the recording modality and electrode technology, see Amplifier Comparison Table). You can combine your EEG recording with other modalities by using the AIM Physiological Monitor, a wireless lightweight amplifier equipped with 6 bipolar and 2 AUX inputs for measuring ExG (i.e., EMG, ECG), GSR, temperature, respiration, heart rate (HR), pulse and SpO2. For example, if you are working in the EEG-TMS field, you want a system that can record the full signal even during stimulation and the **actiCHamp Plus** will surely fit your needs well (measurement range of ±409.6 mV at 0.0487 µV/bit). However, dedicated BrainAmp ExG units are required should you want to record peripheral physiological signals together with your EEG. Or perhaps you will **work in a field (e.g., EEG-fMRI) where passive electrodes** and the BrainAmp family amplifiers may be your only option. In particular, the BrainAmp MR plus could be the perfect choice if EEG-fMRI recordings and lab-based measurements are planned, because it allows you to change resolution, measurement range and cut off frequencies based on your recording environment. Emblem EEG-fNIRSFor such simultaneous recordings, we recommend the **actiCHamp Plus** for lab-based measurements, or the **LiveAmp** for mobile investigations. Nevertheless, the **actiCHamp Plus** could now be a valid alternative for you thanks to its high sampling rates, the flexibility to combine it with active or passive gel-based electrode technologies, and the possibility of expanding your setup for real-time brain-state dependent stimulation. The TurboLink accesses the data recorded by actiCHamp family amplifiers and transmits it reliably via Ethernet in less than 1.5 ms to any compatible online signal processor (e.g., the bossdevice RESEARCH by sync2brain). The **BrainAmp family** will offer you the cleanest stationary setup:  each participant is connected to dedicated amplifier unit(s) that transmit(s) to the BUA, which synchronizes the data and sends them to the recording computer with no need to further work on data re-alignment offline.
